This appeal arises out of judgment and award passed in MVC No.868/2016 by the Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Saundatti (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.868/2016 dated 24.03.2017.
2. Brief facts of the case are that the deceased in this case was working as a driver, driving a truck bearing Regn. No.KA-22/C-1495 belonging to one Mohan Devendrappa Angadi.
On 08.10.2015 at about 8 p.m., the deceased Nagappa Sannammanagar and one Krishna Basappa Hamabar together were walking by the left side of Belagavi-Bagalkote road, to take food in nearby Dabha.

When they were at a distance of about 100 feet away from the petrol pump at that time KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA- 42-F-1637 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life came from their back side and due to such driving, driver of KSRTC bus lost control over bus and dashed to the deceased from behind.
As a result, deceased fell down and bus rolled on his head, as a result, he died at the spot of accident at about 8.15 p.m.
Hence, a claim petition was filed by the petitioners-claimants who are the legal representatives of the deceased.
3. Before the Tribunal in order to prove the case, claimants got examined two witnesses as PW1 and PW2 and got marked 9 documents as Ex.P1 to P9.
On the other hand, the respondent-KSRTC got examined one witness as RW1 and got marked documents as EX.R1 to R4 in its favour.

4. After hearing the learned counsels for both the sides and on assessment of oral as well as documentary evidence, Tribunal allowed the claim petition in part, filed by the respondents/claimants and awarded compensation of Rs.41,30,000/- with interest at the rate of 9%
per annum from the date petition till the date of realization.
Aggrieved by the said award,

respondent-KSRTC preferred this appeal, praying to modify the judgment and award passed in MVC No.868/2016 considering contributory negligence of the deceased and in respect of quantum of compensation awarded.
5. We have heard the learned counsel for the appellant- KSRTC and learned counsel for respondents/claimants and perused the material on record.

6. Learned counsel for the appellant vehemently contended that the Tribunal has totally erred by allowing the claim petition filed by the respondents/claimants, by fixing the liability on the appellant and also in respect of the quantum of the compensation awarded.
He would further contend that the alleged accident took place due to the negligence of the deceased.

The witness The Divisional Controller vs Smt. Renuka W/O Appanna Sa Sannammanavr on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198003242/
3 RW-1 examined on behalf of the KSRTC has categorically deposed to that effect before the Court that the deceased and two other persons had consumed alcohol and were walking on the road haphazardly without observing the vehicles moving on the road.

sentences.text: Though, the bus driver made his best efforts to avoid the accident, the deceased himself suddenly came in the middle of the road and caused the accident.

According to the learned counsel, the said aspect was very much brought to the knowledge of the Deputy Superintendent of Police and Superintendent of Police, Ramadurga by way of lodging a complaint through RPAD.
The postal acknowledgements were also marked before the Tribunal as per Ex.R2 to R4.
The Tribunal failed to consider that aspect.
7. Learned counsel would further contend that the doctor who conducted autopsy over the dead body of the deceased has issued two postmortem reports.

Initially, after conducting the autopsy,
doctor issued postmortem report as per Ex.P.6 on 10.10.2015 which is marked in the evidence of claimants/respondents.
Wherein, the doctor opined that the death is due hemorrhage shock and cardio respiratory failure due to multiple fractures of bones and due to RTA.

Nevertheless, the same doctor has also issued one more postmortem report dated 17.10.2015 based on the request of the appellant-KSRTC, wherein the opinion of the doctor reveals that the death is due to hemorrhage shock and cardio respiratory failure due to multiple fractures of brain and alcoholic consumption.
Further, in the said report, on examination of abdomen, the doctor found the presence of alcohol contents in the stomach.

Hence, according to the learned counsel, by perusal of the evidence of the RW-1 coupled with medical report dated 17.10.2015, it clearly depicts that the death is due to negligence of the deceased himself.

The learned counsel would further contend that though, the counsel for the appellant-KSRTC failed to mark the said postmortem report before the Tribunal,
nevertheless, the same is very much available on record.
Inspite of that, Tribunal failed to consider the same and fixed the liability on the respondent which is totally unsustainable in law.
8. Further, the counsel would contend that the Tribunal erred in assessing the compensation to be awarded.

More particularly, the Tribunal erred in taking the income of the deceased at Rs.25,000/-
per month only by relying on the driving license and without any supporting documents to that effect.
Further, the Tribunal has granted 9% interest per annum from the date of petition till realization on the compensation amount, which is also on higher side.
Accordingly, learned counsel for the appellant contend that the Tribunal is not justified in passing the award both on fixing liability and quantum of compensation.

Hence, he prays to set aside the judgment and award dated 24.03.2017.
9.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents / claimants would contend that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal impugned under this appeal does not suffer from any perversity or illegality and the Tribunal passed the award on proper appreciation of the evidence and material available on record.

He would further contend that by perusal of Ex.P6-postmortem report issued on 10.10.2015, clearly depicts that death is due to hemorrhage shock and cardio respiratory failure due to multiple fractures of brain and due to RTA, as a result of the accident caused by the driver of the KSRTC bus.
Moreover, the appellant-KSRTC failed to produce and mark one more postmortem report which is available on record for the reasons best known to them.
Though, RW.1 was examined on behalf of the Corporation, they failed to mark the said postmortem report and therefore they cannot be relied upon.

Hence, according to the learned counsel, Tribunal has rightly The Divisional Controller vs Smt. Renuka W/O Appanna Sa Sannammanavr on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198003242/
4 fixed the liability on the appellant- KSRTC.

sentences.text: He would further contend that the Tribunal is justified in awarding the compensation in all the components including the income of the deceased.

He would further contend that jurisdictional Police filed charge sheet as per Ex.P7 which clearly depicts that the accident was caused due to the negligence of driver of the bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1637.

Hence, he prays to dismiss the appeal filed by the appellant-KSRTC.
- 10 - 10.
We have bestowed our anxious consideration on the submission made by the learned counsel for both the sides and perused the material available on record including trial Court records.

11. Having heard both sides & on perusal of records, it is evident that accident took place on 08.10.2015 at about 8.15 p.m. at Belagavi-Bagalkote road, near Dhaba in which the deceased died and also it is not in dispute that the driver of the KSRTC Bus has caused the said accident by dashing the deceased from back side.

Hence, the only point that arise for our consideration is that "Whether the deceased also contributed his negligence for the accident?"
12.
Admittedly, the accident took place in the night hours at 8 p.m.

It is also not in dispute that as per the contents of the complaint lodged by the relative of the deceased as per Ex.P.2 that the deceased and two other persons were walking on the road at the time of accident.
It is the contention of the appellant-KSRTC that the deceased and - 11 - two other persons have consumed alcohol and were walking on the road haphazardly.
Though, the driver of the bus made his best efforts to avoid accident, however, due to negligence of the deceased who strayed into the middle of the road, he came under the wheels of the bus.

To substantiate the said aspect, appellant-KSRTC lodged complaint to the Dy. Superintendent of Police and Superintendent of Police,
Ramaduraga by lodging complaint through RPAD.

Postal acknowledgments are marked in the evidence of RW-1 as per Ex.R3 and R4.
13.

No doubt the appellant-KSRTC failed to mark the postmortem report obtained by the doctor who conducted autopsy over the dead body dated 17.10.2015, by confronting it to the witness examined on behalf of the claimants or in the evidence of the RW.1.

But at the same time it is evident that the doctor has issued two postmortem reports dated 10.10.2015 and 17.10.2015, wherein the second opinion as to the cause of death is given i.e at the time of accident, the deceased had - 12 - consumed the alcohol.
On examination of the abdomen, the doctor found alcohol presence in the stomach and its contents.

Due regard should have been given to The Divisional Controller vs Smt. Renuka W/O Appanna Sa Sannammanavr on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198003242/
5 Ex.P6 and subsequent postmortem available on record and also the Ex.P3 and P4 postal acknowledgements for having lodged the complaint through RPAD by the KSRTC in respect of the accident where it was alleged that the same is caused due to the negligence of the deceased.

sentences.text: Hence, in our considered opinion, matter requires re-consideration by the Tribunal.

Even otherwise, the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal more particularly, on the head of income of the deceased only by relying on the driving license of the deceased and taking income of the deceased at Rs.25,000/- per month and also awarding interest at 9% per annum have to be reconsidered with proper documentary evidence.

14. In the facts and circumstances, matter requires reconsideration both on fixing liability i.e. negligence contributed if any by the deceased for the accident and - 13 - also on the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal on different components.

Hence, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

(i) The Judgment and award dated 24.03.2016 passed in MVC No.868/2016 by the Senior Civil Judge and AMACT, Saundatti is set aside;
(ii) The matter is remanded back to the MACT for reconsideration, by giving opportunity to both sides to lead further evidence if any and to produce any other documents.

(iii) The parties are directed to appear before the Senior Civil Judge and AMACT,
Saundatti on 17.04.2023 without waiting for further notice.
